title: Rowan's docket refuses without naming what unlocks it, so nobody retries
body:
"Rowan's Winter Return Docket" at Albany Civic Center is listed on the local job board, correctly refuses to run, and never tells the player why. Six sessions attempted it and reported it as a broken job. It is not broken — it is silent.

## Settled mechanically, not statistically

The docket (`local_jobs` id `albany_city__civic_core__job`) has FOUR authored options in a clean 2x2: {public, protected} x {byre held, evacuated}. Each requires, beyond the POI and contact the player already visited:

1. the charter-backlog event `albany_city__civic_core__event` RESOLVED, choosing `open_public_relief_record` or `protect_household_relief_details`; and
2. `wolf_winter` COMPLETED, which grants `fact:wolf_winter_byre_held` XOR `fact:wolf_winter_steading_evacuated` through the quest's `campaign_exports`.

`tests/starting_slice/winter_return_docket_counterfactual.test.ts` already proves this exhaustively and is green: one case walks all 16 Wolf-Winter campaign exports crossed with both event options — 32 combinations — and asserts `availableLocalJobSceneOptions` returns EXACTLY ONE legal option every time, with held XOR evacuated for every export. There is no reachable non-death outcome that leaves the docket empty. So this is not a content gap and must not be "fixed" by authoring more options.

## The actual defect

The player is told to choose an option and shown none, with no statement of what would unlock one. The listing does not name the prerequisites, and the rejection does not either — `12c5f2b4` improved the rejection's wording ("no authored option is legal yet") without naming what is missing. A player who has scouted the POI and talked to the contact has done everything the surface asked of them and still sees nothing, so they reasonably file it as broken. Six sessions did.

This is the same class as bug_0617 (the paused-gameplay event lead that reported engine vocabulary instead of the pending decision) and bug_0618 (the Store-Shed ladder citing a "currently listed yearling action" that was listed nowhere): a block that is mechanically right and informationally empty. Fixing it once per instance is how we got three of them.

## The behaviour that sets the acceptance criterion

The playtest lane reconstructed the call timelines for all six docket sessions. Every refusal happened while Wolf-Winter was still incomplete, which confirms the analysis above. But the decisive fact is what the players did next: **each attempted the docket exactly once and never retried** — including four who went on to complete Wolf-Winter and other quests in the same run, and one who afterwards passed `option_id` correctly to a different job, so this was not API confusion.

That rules out the cheap fix. A refusal that merely reports an empty legal-option set is still a dead end: it tells the player nothing has changed and gives them no reason to return, so the observed behaviour — one attempt, then never again — would survive it unchanged. Four players in this corpus were holding the unlock in their hands later in the same session and never went back.

**Acceptance criterion:** the unlock must be stated, in the player's terms, in BOTH surfaces:

- the LISTING, so a player who cannot work it yet learns why it is on the board at all; and
- the REJECTION, so a player who tries anyway leaves with a reason to come back.

The words to say are the two real prerequisites: resolve the charter-backlog event at the civic-core POI, and complete Wolf-Winter. A fix that changes only the rejection text, or that names the gate in engine vocabulary rather than in something a player can act on, does not close this.

## What would close it

Name the unmet prerequisite in the rejection and, if the surface allows, in the listing: the charter-backlog filing decision, and the Wolf-Winter return. The data to say so is already present at the point of refusal — the scene declares `requires_resolved_events` and each option declares `requires_event_options` / `requires_all_world_facts`, so the code can report WHICH gate failed rather than that some gate did.

Prefer the class-level move if one is available: the three bugs above all reach the player through blocked-lead / locked-action copy paths that know the failing condition and discard it. A shared "name the unmet gate" helper would close the class rather than the third instance of it.

## Cross-references

- `intake/queue` P1 playtest/bug `56b3d1a6260af50c` — "Albany Rowan docket appears without executable job options", 3 Terra reports plus 2 runner-enforced Sonnet sessions.
- qa/tickets `S2-bug-3c86bd6dd9e5109f` @ `albany_city`, the triage cluster for the same defect.
- Engine proof that the docket is completable: `tests/starting_slice/winter_return_docket_counterfactual.test.ts`.

evidence.summary: Six sessions attempted it once and never retried; four completed Wolf-Winter later in the same run. The docket is completable (proved exhaustively) but names neither prerequisite.
